items.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
items.summary: The paper proposes Latent Lattice Language Models, adding horizontal latent streams per layer to boost computational capacity instead of deeper layers.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a new way to scale models, potentially improving efficiency and performance for advanced NLP tasks.

items.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
items.summary: ViRA introduces CrossRPO, a reinforcement learning method that trains visual agents to read evidence in ultra‑high‑resolution images instead of guessing.
items.whyItMatters: It improves accuracy of AI image‑question systems, crucial for applications needing precise visual evidence.

items.title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
items.summary: The study evaluates how National Hurricane Center forecaster discussions improve tropical cyclone intensity predictions beyond numerical models.
items.whyItMatters: It shows human insight can enhance forecast accuracy, informing better preparedness and resource allocation.

items.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
items.summary: The article explains how vision‑language models decide the order of object descriptions in an image.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this planning reveals how VLMs process visual scenes, improving interpretability and guiding future model design.

items.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
items.summary: Hyperlyve is a framework that verifies asymptotic stability of nonlinear systems with neural network controllers by learning CPA Lyapunov functions via CEGIS.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable, formal method to certify safety of AI‑controlled dynamics, crucial for reliable autonomous systems.

items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
items.summary: The paper explores using evolutionarily generated specialist neural networks as reusable memory to prevent catastrophic forgetting in continual reinforcement learning.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a novel, biologically inspired approach to maintain performance across changing environments.

items.title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
items.summary: The paper presents a bagging algorithm that learns an autoregressive next-token model from chain-of-thought demonstrations, achieving optimal sample efficiency for binary tokens.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it improves training efficiency and reliability of large language models using CoT data.

items.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
items.summary: The paper shows that in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures, a shared component in encoder outputs causes representation collapse, which batch-normalized projectors fail to fix.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this flaw helps improve self-supervised learning models.

items.title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
items.summary: The article describes fitting BSIM4 parameters to 77 K I‑V data of SKY130 transistors using a neural surrogate of NGSpice for compact modeling.
items.whyItMatters: Accurate cryogenic models enable reliable simulation of low‑temperature circuits, critical for space and quantum computing applications.

items.title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
items.summary: The paper uses deep learning and transformer models to analyze early-career tech job ads, clustering roles beyond titles to reveal industry differences.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers can better navigate career paths and hiring trends with nuanced role insights.

items.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
items.summary: CertiSum ensures bitwise-identical MXFP4 training across different parallelism layouts and GPU vendors.
items.whyItMatters: It stabilizes debugging and auditability for low‑precision AI models.

items.title: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises
items.summary: ScenarioForge automates turning high-level cyber exercise requirements into deployable, verifiable scenarios, reducing manual setup of infrastructure, services, and success conditions.
items.whyItMatters: It speeds up cyber-range creation, enabling faster, more realistic training for security teams.

items.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as…

items.title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
items.summary: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates. Based on Shapley values, DynSurvX introduces a hierarchical two-phase strategy…

items.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
items.summary: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. Because histology images lack a canonical orientation, D_4 TTA---pooling across the 8 rotations and reflections of a square---is a standard default in computational pathology. However, the rise of self-supervised histology foundation models (FMs) with inherent rotational…

items.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
items.summary: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where…

items.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
items.summary: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from…

items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.summary: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. In this work, we present a rigorous benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks…

items.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
items.summary: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required. Here we present the R package ONAM, which provides a novel and practical implementation of functional decomposition, a technique to facilitate…

items.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
items.summary: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection.
